- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.16) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the forecast by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is positive (especially > 0.27) and forecast is trending down, adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.  
- Model tends to overestimate early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to first 5–7 days.  
- After a strong price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +10% above prior peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model tends to underestimate — add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for 3–5 days ahead.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative and price is trending down, model often fails to capture mean reversion — add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to mid-horizon (days 10–20).
